question: Why do the best Japanese swords still need tatara steel?
answer: The mill wins the race, but every bit of its steel is the same. The tatara, lit one night a year in Shimane as it was 1300 years ago, gives a carbon spread and impurities that mass production can't copy. That uneven, impure character is why the best Japanese swords still need tatara steel.
move: Faster and more uniform is not always better steel.

web.label: Two steel furnaces race side by side: a modern mill makes fast, even steel, while the ancient tatara makes slow, uneven steel. The page asks why the best Japanese swords still need tatara steel.

source: Veritasium, “How Japanese Masters Turn Sand Into Swords” (YouTube, 2024)
